newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower as correction continues.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower as correction continues.

text.p: Milan shares ended lower on Tuesday continuing Monday's correction as stocks sought to find a level to consolidate around after last week's strong gains, and due to concern over a delay in the single European currency.

Dealers said that the high value of the dollar was continuing to cause some concern while a lower opening to Wall Street gave no clear lead to Milan stocks. The government and unions had their last meeting on welfare spending ahead of the summer break. dealers noted.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 2.24 percent at 14,637 and the blue chip Mib30 2.29 percent down at 22,234.

There was market concern after comments from German government advisor Rolf Peffekoven who said a two year delay for EMU would be preferable to starting with a weak euro on the current schedule for 1999. While Treasury Minister Ciampi said the dollar rise did not pose a threat to Italy's inflation rate.
Blue chips generally lower with ENI losing early gains to end off 1.37 percent at 10,484 lire, Fiat off 4.26 percent at 6,050 lire and Pirelli down 3.49 percent at 4,889 lire.
Ambroveneto off 2.92 percent at 9,552 lire after the charity that owns savings bank Cariplo said late Monday it had given its formal approval to Cariplo-Ambroveneto merger.

The charity foundation will eventually hold 29 percent of the parent which will control Cariplo and Ambroveneto, and the foundation will participate in Ambroveneto's planned capital increase of up to 6.8 trillion lire over five years.
Also in banking stocks, San Paolo continues lower after Monday's Goldman Sachs downgrade with the shares ending off 3.92 percent at 13,590 lire.

Automotive brake maker Brembo ended off 4.72 percent at 19,661 lire after reporting at its annual meeting that first half 1997 performance was in line with its own forecasts and it was eyeing expansion in China.
